title: Lock a bayonet cap into its socket
instruction: Pick up the blue cap by its square head, line its orange lugs up with the slots in the round socket on the grey box, push it down, and turn it a quarter turn counterclockwise until it stops.
context: Bayonet mounts close battery compartments, lamp sockets, filter housings and quarter-turn connectors (O*NET 49-2094.00, 51-2028.00). Unlike screwing on a thread, the cap must be turned to match a keyed opening, pushed against a spring and turned to a stop.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). Box: grey PLA 12 x 7 x 2.5 cm, 150 g, standing on a fixed grey 4 x 5 x 2 cm block centred at x 21, y -5, both turned 45 degrees clockwise seen from above. A round socket sits 3.4 cm in front of the box centre along its long axis: a 2.6 cm opening in a 4 mm roof, with two 6 mm wide slots along the box's long axis reaching 1.9 cm from the socket centre, over a chamber with two stops that let the cap turn only counterclockwise, up to just past 90 degrees. Under the opening, an orange PLA plate (2.2 x 2.2 cm) rides on a spring (1.5 N per mm, 6 mm travel) 3 mm below the roof's underside. Cap: blue PLA, 30 g: a 2.4 cm diameter, 2 cm tall barrel, a 2 x 2 x 2 cm square grip head on top, and two orange lugs (5 x 6 x 5 mm) sticking out 1.7 cm from its axis near the barrel's bottom; it stands upright on the table at x 12, y 15, lugs turned 30 degrees clockwise from the arms' forward direction.
scoring: Measured at the end from a top photo and a ruler. 0 if the box was at any point moved more than 3 cm, tilted more than 20 degrees or turned more than 20 degrees. Otherwise: 1.0 if the cap is locked: its axis within 3 mm of the socket centre, upright within 10 degrees, lugs turned more than 80 degrees from the slots and held up against the roof's underside (cap within 1.5 mm of that height), and still (moving less than 1 mm and 2 degrees over 1 s), for 1 s; 0.75 if, with the lugs pushed below the roof, the cap was turned more than 45 degrees; 0.5 if, after being lifted, the cap was pushed in with its lugs below the roof's underside; 0.25 if the cap was lifted 3 cm; else 0.
reset_notes: Turn the cap back clockwise to the slots, lift it out, and stand it on its mark with its lugs at the marked angle; set the box on its foot in its marked outline.
fidelity: Rigid bodies built from boxes and a cylinder; the foot is fixed. Lugs, slots, roof and stops are real colliders, so locking comes from contact alone; the spring is a prismatic joint with a spring drive and no preload. Contact offsets are 0.5 mm and light angular damping is added to the parts so the 1 mm fits do not chatter. No contact force cap is enforced in simulation.
